reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Adult lateral neck mass: metastatic until proven
Thyroglossal moves with tongue; Sistrunk includes hyoid
Left supraclavicular node: abdomen and chest primary
reference.pathophysiology: Persistent HPV or EBV driven mucosal cancers shed cells to jugular nodes while thyroglossal tracts persist from thyroid descent and second arch clefts fail to obliterate; thoracic duct returns left sided lymph (and gastric or lung tumour emboli) to venous angle at level IV.
additionalDifferentials: Thyroglossal versus dermoid by tongue movement
Branchial cyst versus nodal metastasis by age and solidity
Radical versus selective dissection by nodal burden
additionalInvestigations: Nasendoscopy and full head neck examination
Ultrasound guided FNAC with HPV, EBV, thyroglobulin
Contrast CT or MRI neck plus chest for unknown primary
